-- ─── VERSION ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- The authoritative version string, and the one every comparison uses. -- -- MUSHclient stores a plugin's `version` attribute as a NUMBER, so -- GetPluginInfo(id, 19) cannot return "6.0.1" -- it comes back as 6, which is -- why the load banner read "v6". Anything comparing that against the published -- VERSION file sees a permanent mismatch: the update banner would never clear -- and the plugin file would be re-fetched on every check. -- -- This, not the <plugin version="..."> attribute, is the plugin's version. -- -- MUSHclient parses that attribute as a number and refuses to load the plugin -- at all if it has more than one decimal place -- "6.0.1" is rejected outright -- with "Too many decimal places". So the attribute can only ever carry -- major.minor, and everything that actually compares versions reads this -- instead. -- -- Keep it in step with the VERSION file; tests/version_consistency_test.lua -- fails the build if they disagree, and checks the attribute is the -- major.minor of it. SND_VERSION = "6.0.2-dev"
-- snd_version() also exists in constants.lua, for the modules to call: modules -- are updated by 'snd update' while this file is not, so a module calling a -- function that lives only here would break any install running an older -- plugin file. -- -- This file cannot call that one, though. The update path runs -- _snd_update_plugin_file_if_stale() the instant the module downloads finish, -- which is before the new modules have been loaded -- and on an install whose -- constants.lua predates snd_version(), the global is simply not there. That -- is a run-time error in the middle of an update. So the XML reads the -- constant directly and never depends on a module being present. local function _snd_version_str() return tostring(SND_VERSION or PLUGIN_VERSION or "?") end
-- ─── REMOTE SOURCE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- Everything the plugin downloads -- itself, its modules, the manifest, the -- seed data, the sounds -- comes from one repository. These two lines are the -- only place that repository is named; every URL below is derived from them, -- so moving hosts is a two-line change rather than a hunt through three files. -- -- SND_RAW_URL takes the branch first and the repo-relative path second. The -- path shape differs by host, which is why the whole pattern is configurable -- and not just the domain: -- -- GitHub https://raw.githubusercontent.com/USER/REPO/%s/%s -- Gitea https://HOST/USER/REPO/~files/%s/%s -- SND_RAW_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AardCrowley/Search-and-Destroy-Revamp/%s/%s"
-- The branch modules, the manifest, the changelog and the seed data are served -- from. The plugin file itself is pulled from a "v<version>" TAG instead, by -- download_plugin, so a user updating gets an immutable release rather than -- whatever master happens to hold at that moment. SND_BRANCH = "main"
-- Where 'snd dev update' pulls from. A branch, not a tag: the point is to test -- work in progress without cutting a release for it. SND_DEV_BRANCH = "dev"
-- Repo-relative path -> full raw URL. `branch` overrides SND_BRANCH, which is -- what the updater uses to pull a specific release. function snd_raw_url(path, branch) return string.format(SND_RAW_URL, branch or SND_BRANCH, path) end
versionURL = snd_raw_url("VERSION") CHANGELOG_URL = snd_raw_url("changelog.md")

It was persisted -- by the changelog code but never read back, so it was nil on every load -- and the "what changed since your version" path could never run. last_installed_version = snd_get_setting("last_installed_version", "") -- Which branch the last update came from. The version string alone cannot -- answer this: a development build is not obliged to carry a distinct -- version, so someone running 'snd dev update' against an unbumped tree -- would look identical to a release install. snd_update_channel = snd_get_setting("snd_update_channel", "") apply_xset_gqalias() end
-- ─── LIFECYCLE HANDLERS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The mapper broadcasts the path it just found on channel 502, as -- "found_paths = { ... }" in Lua table syntax, synchronously from inside -- findpath(). That is the only way a table can cross between plugins: -- CallPlugin carries strings and numbers, not tables. -- -- Only the capture lives here. The bridge that uses it is in pathing.lua, so -- that a module calling it still works on an install whose plugin file predates -- this -- the global simply stays nil and the BFS is used instead. _snd_mapper_path_raw = nil
-- Every leg of the route, not just the last. -- -- findpath broadcasts once per path it completes -- but when the source room -- forbids portalling it does not complete one. It walks to the nearest room it -- can jump from, calls itself for that leg, calls itself again for the rest, -- concatenates the two and returns WITHOUT broadcasting the total. Only the -- recursive calls broadcast. Keeping just the last one therefore measured the -- second leg alone and silently dropped the walk out -- in exactly the case -- the walk-out is the thing being measured. _snd_mapper_path_parts = {}
function OnPluginBroadcast(msg, id, name, text) if msg == 502 and id == PLUGIN_ID_MAPPER then _snd_mapper_path_raw = text _snd_mapper_path_parts[#_snd_mapper_path_parts + 1] = text end
if id == _GMCP_HANDLER_ID then if text == "char.status" then current_character_state = gmcp("char.status.state") local lvl = tonumber(gmcp("char.status.level")) if lvl and lvl < 200 and anex_automatic_onoff == "on" then if type(anex_check_tnl_silent) == "function" then anex_check_tnl_silent() end end elseif text == "char.base" then if type(resolve_pending_character) == "function" then resolve_pending_character(gmcp("char.base.name")) end elseif text == "room.info" then sound_not_played = true local ri = gmcp("room.info") if ri then ri.maze = (ri.details and ri.details:find("maze") ~= nil) and 1 or 0 previous_room = current_room or {rmid = "-2", arid = "-2"} current_room = {rmid = ri.num, arid = ri.zone, exits = ri.exits, maze = ri.maze, name = ri.name} if current_room.rmid ~= previous_room.rmid then if going_to_room == current_room.rmid then if type(action_on_destination_arrived) == "function" then action_on_destination_arrived() end going_to_room = nil end if #room_history == 300 then table.remove(room_history) end table.insert(room_history, 1, room_history[0]) room_history[0] = {rmid = current_room.rmid, arid = current_room.arid} end if current_room.arid ~= previous_room.arid then if type(check_zone_known) == "function" then check_zone_known(current_room.arid) end end end elseif text == "comm.quest" then if type(quest_status_gmcp) == "function" then quest_status_gmcp(gmcp("comm.quest")) end elseif text == "config" then noexp_onoff = (gmcp("config.noexp") == "YES") and "on" or "off" end elseif id == _Z_ORDER_ID and msg == 996 and text == "re-register z" then if type(xg_create_window) == "function" then xg_create_window() end end end
function OnPluginInstall() local json_ok json_ok, json = pcall(require, "json") if not json_ok then ColourNote("white", "red", "SnD: 'json' library not available: " .. tostring(json)) end _snd_bootstrap(function() if type(init_plugin_after_load) == "function" then init_plugin_after_load() end end) end
function OnPluginEnable() if type(InfoNote) == "function" then InfoNote("Enabled ", "Search and Destroy") end if type(xg_create_window) == "function" then xg_create_window() end end
function OnPluginDisable() if type(InfoNote) == "function" then InfoNote("Disabled ", "Search and Destroy") end if type(xg_destroy_window) == "function" then xg_destroy_window() end end -- Alias handler: 'snd changelog [all|since <version>]' -- -- Replaces the previous JSON-based implementation, which never worked: it was -- only ever called with all_changes=true so the version-diff branch was dead, -- last_installed_version was written but never read back so it was nil on -- every load anyway, and the URL pointed at a JSON file that does not exist. -- Parsing and rendering now live in changelog.lua; this is just the entry point. function get_changelog(mode, req_version) if type(mode) == "boolean" then mode = mode and "all" or "new" end if type(cl_show) ~= "function" then ErrorNote("SnD: changelog.lua is not loaded.") return end cl_show(mode or "new", req_version) end

snd_set_setting("gqid_joined", gqid_joined, false) DebugNote("Joined gq ", gqid_joined, " gqid_started ", gqid_started) if (gqid_joined == gqid_started) then EnableTriggerGroup("trg_gqmsg", true) do_gq_info() end end

function gqmsg_declared(name, line, wildcards) -- "Global Quest: Global quest # N has been declared for levels X to Y." -- Informational only; player decides whether to join. DebugNote("GQ declared: #", wildcards.gq_id, " levels ", wildcards.min_lvl, "-", wildcards.max_lvl) end
function gqmsg_completed_other(name, line, wildcards) -- "Global Quest: PlayerName has completed Global Quest # N." -- Another player finished in extended time; our quest continues. DebugNote("GQ completed by ", wildcards.winner, " (gq #", wildcards.gq_id, ")") end
function gqmsg_started(name, line, wildcards) -- "The global quest for levels X to Y has now started." has no gq_id. -- If we've joined a GQ, this start message is for it. if gqid_joined ~= "-1" then gqid_started = gqid_joined snd_set_setting("gqid_started", gqid_started, false) EnableTriggerGroup("trg_gqmsg", true) do_gq_info() end end
-- [[ Gquest check functions ]] -- do_gq_info / send_gq_info / on_gq_info_captured / on_gq_info_parsed are now -- in lua/targets.lua and use Capture.untagged_output. function send_gq_check() -- Thin wrapper kept for backward-compat; do_gq_check handles debug mode. do_gq_check() end
function gqmsg_winner(name, line, wildcards) -- "The global quest has been won by Name - Nth win." has no gq_id. local winner = wildcards.winner local you = gmcp("char.base.name") if (winner == you) then ColourNote("#FFFFFF", "", "\nA WINNER IS YOU\n") -- Enable GQ reward mode so the reward triggers fill _gq_* accumulators. -- Delay the history_end call by 0.75s to let the reward lines arrive first. if type(gq_reward_mode_on) == "function" then gq_reward_mode_on() end DoAfterSpecial(0.75, "gq_end_won()", sendto.script) elseif gqid_joined ~= "-1" then -- Someone else won; we're still in our GQ which may go to extended time. EnableTrigger("trg_gqmsg_extended_time", true) DoAfterSpecial(0.5, "gq_check_if_extended()", sendto.script) end end
function gqmsg_extended_time(name, line, wildcards) -- "The global quest will go into extended time for N more minutes." has no gq_id. if gqid_joined ~= "-1" then gqid_extended = gqid_joined end end
function gq_check_if_extended() EnableTrigger("trg_gqmsg_extended_time", false) if (gqid_extended ~= gqid_joined) then gq_end_failed() end end

function gq_ended(name, line, wildcards) if gqid_joined == wildcards.gq_id then gq_end_timeout() end end
function xcp_set_action_mode(name, line, wildcards) local opt = wildcards.option or "" local options = { ["ht"] = "ht - do hunt trick", ["qw"] = "qw - do quick where", ["off"] = "off - no additional action" } if (opt == "ht") or (opt == "qw") or (opt == "off") then xcp_action_mode = opt snd_set_setting("xcp_action_mode", opt, false) InfoNote("Set 'xcp' mode to: ", options[opt], ".") elseif (opt == "") then InfoNote("Current 'xcp' mode: " .. options[xcp_action_mode] .. ".") InfoNote("Syntax: 'xcp mode [ht|qw|off]'") else InfoNote("Invalid 'xcp' mode given. Syntax: 'xcp mode [ht|qw|off]'") end print("") end

InfoNote("\nxcp quest targeting is now ", string.upper(xcp_targets_quest_onoff)) end

It is what ranks the results by where that mob has actually been -- seen, so offering the syntax and ignoring it made the list look unsorted. function map_area(name, line, wildcards) local w = (type(wildcards) == "table" and wildcards) or {} search_rooms_fuzzy(w.loc, current_room.arid, w.mob) end
function map_area_all(name, line, wildcards) local w = (type(wildcards) == "table" and wildcards) or {} search_rooms_fuzzy(w.loc, nil, w.mob) end
-- [[ "xwhere" command ]] function do_xwhere(name, line, wildcards) local n1 = tonumber(wildcards.n1) or 12 -- if no number given, default to 12 local n2 = tonumber(wildcards.n2) or "" local mob = wildcards.mob or "" if (mob == "") then -- user entered no numbers, no mobname, or no args at all InfoNote("\nSearch and Destroy: 'xwhere' required parameter missing.\n") InfoNote(" Syntax: 'xwhere <mobname>'") InfoNote(" 'xwhere <n1> <mobname>'") -- where 1.mobname to n1.mobname InfoNote(" 'xwhere <n1> <n2> <mobname>'") -- where 1.mobname to n2.mobname return elseif (n2 == "") then -- user entered one number (n1) and a mobname, but no second number (n2) InfoNote("\nSearch and Destroy: 'xwhere ", n1, " ", mob, "'") for i = 1, n1, 1 do if (i == 1) then Send("where " .. mob) else Send("where " .. i .. "." .. mob) end end elseif (mob ~= "") and (n2 ~= "") then -- user entered n1, n2, and mobname InfoNote("Search and Destroy: 'xwhere ", n1, " ", n2, " ", mob, "'") for i = n1, n2, 1 do if (i == 1) then Send("where " .. mob) else Send("where " .. i .. "." .. mob) end end else InfoNote("Search and Destroy: 'xwhere' data entry problem!") end end
-- [[ Autohunt ]] function auto_hunt(name, line, wildcards) local s = string.lower(wildcards.arg) if (s == "abort") or (s == "cancel") or (s == "0") then auto_hunt_abort() else ht_reset() EnableTriggerGroup("AutoHunt", true) auto_hunt_mob = s Send("hunt " .. s) end end

function auto_hunt_lowskill() InfoNote("\nSearch and Destroy: Autohunt not available - hunt skill is too low.") InfoNote(" If hunt skill is available, practice it to 85% or higher.") auto_hunt_reset() end

function auto_hunt_next(name, line, wildcards) local dir = wildcards.dir auto_hunt_move(dir) Send("hunt " .. auto_hunt_mob) end

Reports each step -- separately so a failure says which one. function xtest_findpath(name, line, wildcards) local w = (type(wildcards) == "table" and wildcards) or {} local src = tonumber(w.src) or tonumber(gmcp("room.info.num")) local dst = tonumber(w.dst) if not src or not dst then InfoNote("SnD: usage: xtest findpath [<src>] <dst>") return end
InfoNote("SnD: findpath probe src=", tostring(src), " dst=", tostring(dst))
_snd_mapper_path_raw = nil local t0 = os.clock() local ok, rc = pcall(CallPlugin, PLUGIN_ID_MAPPER, "findpath", tostring(src), tostring(dst)) local t_call = os.clock() - t0
InfoNote("SnD: pcall ok : ", tostring(ok)) InfoNote("SnD: CallPlugin returned: ", tostring(rc), " (non-zero is expected -- findpath returns a table, which", " CallPlugin cannot marshal back)") InfoNote("SnD: 502 broadcast seen : ", tostring(_snd_mapper_path_raw ~= nil))
-- Timed separately so the two numbers are comparable: the mapper searches -- the database, ours walks an in-memory graph, and the whole reason the -- in-memory graph exists is that the first was slow. local t1 = os.clock() local mh = (type(snd_mapper_hops) == "function") and snd_mapper_hops(src, dst) or nil local t_mapper = os.clock() - t1
local t2 = os.clock() local bh = (type(snd_bfs_hops) == "function") and snd_bfs_hops(src, dst) or nil local t_bfs = os.clock() - t2
InfoNote("SnD: mapper hops : ", tostring(mh), string.format(" (%.3fs)", t_mapper)) InfoNote("SnD: our BFS hops : ", tostring(bh), string.format(" (%.3fs)", t_bfs))
if mh and bh then if mh == bh then InfoNote("SnD: they agree.") else InfoNote("SnD: they differ by ", tostring(math.abs(mh - bh)), " hop(s).") end elseif not mh then InfoNote("SnD: the mapper bridge produced nothing; the BFS stands.") end
-- A hop count only means something once you can see what it counted. local mp = (type(snd_mapper_path) == "function") and snd_mapper_path(src, dst) or nil if mp then InfoNote("SnD: mapper route:") local n = 0 while mp[n + 1] ~= nil do n = n + 1 local step = mp[n] InfoNote(string.format("SnD: %2d. %-22s -> %s", n, tostring(step.dir), tostring(step.uid))) if n >= 25 then InfoNote("SnD: ... (truncated)") break end end end
local bp = (type(snd_bfs_path) == "function") and snd_bfs_path(src, dst) or nil if bp then InfoNote("SnD: our route (rooms only -- the BFS does not track", " directions, the mapper walks it):") for i, step in ipairs(bp) do InfoNote(string.format("SnD: %2d. %-22s -> %s", i, step.via, step.room)) if i >= 25 then InfoNote("SnD: ... (truncated)") break end end end
InfoNote("SnD: a step marked 'portal/recall (assumed usable here)' is the", " assumption to check -- our search allows it from anywhere.") end
-- Whether a room forbids portalling or recalling, straight from the mapper. -- -- This is the whole point of the comparison: our search seeds every portal -- destination at depth 1 from anywhere, so in a room that permits portals we -- and the mapper agree trivially and the run proves nothing. The mapper only -- has to do something different -- walk out to somewhere it can portal from -- -- when the room forbids it. Reporting the flags means the run says whether it -- was the decisive test, instead of leaving it to be inferred from the fact -- that every answer came back identical again. local function _snd_room_portal_flags(uid) if not mapper_db_file or not uid then return nil end local ok, np, nr = pcall(function() local db = sqlite3.open(mapper_db_file) if not db then return nil end local a, b for row in db:nrows("SELECT noportal, norecall FROM rooms WHERE uid=" .. fixsql(tostring(uid)) .. " LIMIT 1") do a, b = tonumber(row.noportal) or 0, tonumber(row.norecall) or 0 end db:close() return a, b end) if not ok then return nil end return np, nr end

" ORDER BY uid LIMIT 20") do rows[#rows + 1] = row end db:close() end) if not ok then InfoNote("SnD: could not read the mapper database.") return end if #rows == 0 then InfoNote("SnD: no noportal rooms recorded in this area (", here, ").") InfoNote("SnD: 'xtest pathcompare' only tells you something new from a", " room where portalling is blocked -- try a clan hall area,", " a quest zone, or anywhere the mapper has flagged noportal.") return end InfoNote("SnD: noportal rooms in ", here, " -- run 'xtest pathcompare'", " standing in one:") for _, r in ipairs(rows) do InfoNote("SnD: ", string.format(" %-8s %s", tostring(r.uid), tostring(r.name))) end end
-- Alias handler: 'xtest pathcompare [<roomid> ...]'. -- -- Runs both searches over a set of real destinations and reports where they -- disagree, and what each costs. With no arguments it uses the rooms of your -- current campaign or gquest targets, which is the case that actually matters: -- those are what the routing order is built from. -- -- Two things it is measuring: -- * accuracy -- our search allows a portal from anywhere, the mapper does -- not, so ours can be short in a noportal area -- * cost -- the in-memory graph exists because mapper pathing was slow, so -- whether it can be used at all depends on what a call costs function xtest_pathcompare(name, line, wildcards) local w = (type(wildcards) == "table" and wildcards) or {} local src = tonumber(gmcp("room.info.num")) if not src then InfoNote("SnD: no current room from GMCP; cannot compare.") return end
local dests, labels = {}, {} local arg = tostring(w.rooms or "") if arg ~= "" then for id in arg:gmatch("%d+") do dests[#dests + 1] = tonumber(id) labels[#labels + 1] = "room " .. id end else -- Most campaign entries are area targets with no room of their own: -- routing aims at the area's anchor room for those, so that is what -- has to be compared. Taking only entries with a roomid left twelve of -- fourteen targets out of the comparison. local skipped = 0 for i, t in ipairs(main_target_list or {}) do if t.is_dead ~= "yes" then local rid = tonumber(t.roomid) local kind = "room" if not rid or rid <= 0 then rid = (type(snd_area_anchor) == "function") and snd_area_anchor(t.arid) or nil kind = "area anchor" end if rid and rid > 0 then dests[#dests + 1] = rid labels[#labels + 1] = string.format("%s [%s]", tostring(t.mob or ("target " .. i)), kind) else skipped = skipped + 1 end end end if skipped > 0 then InfoNote("SnD: ", tostring(skipped), " target(s) have neither a room", " nor an area anchor and cannot be compared.") end end
if #dests == 0 then InfoNote("SnD: nothing to compare. Load a campaign ('cp info') or name", " rooms: 'xtest pathcompare 24391 455'.") return end
local np, nr = _snd_room_portal_flags(src) local flagstr = "" if np ~= nil then flagstr = (np == 1 and " [noportal]" or "") .. (nr == 1 and " [norecall]" or "") if flagstr == "" then flagstr = " [portals allowed]" end end InfoNote("SnD: comparing ", tostring(#dests), " destination(s) from room ", tostring(src), flagstr) InfoNote("SnD: ", string.format("%-30s %7s %7s %7s %7s %s", "target", "mapper", "mapNP", "ours", "diff", "via"))
local agree, differ, unreachable = 0, 0, 0 local np_differs = 0 local routes, multi_leg = {}, 0 local slowest, slowest_i = 0, nil local portalled = 0 local t_mapper_total, t_bfs_total = 0, 0 local worst, worst_i = 0, nil
for i, dst in ipairs(dests) do local t0 = os.clock() -- The route AND its length from one call, so the summary and the -- route printed underneath can never be two different answers. local mroute, mh, mlegs = snd_mapper_route(src, dst) local t_this = os.clock() - t0 t_mapper_total = t_mapper_total + t_this if t_this > slowest then slowest, slowest_i = t_this, i end routes[i] = mroute if mlegs and mlegs > 1 then multi_leg = multi_leg + 1 end
-- The same route with portals forbidden. If this is larger than the -- portal-allowed answer, portals genuinely shorten the trip -- and in -- a room that blocks them, that gap is exactly how much our count -- understates the walk. If it is identical everywhere, the mapper is -- not applying the restriction either and neither of us models it. local mnp = snd_mapper_hops(src, dst, true)
local t1 = os.clock() local bh = snd_bfs_hops(src, dst) t_bfs_total = t_bfs_total + (os.clock() - t1)
-- Whether our answer leans on a portal is the thing worth seeing: a -- portal destination is seeded at depth 1 from anywhere, so any target -- nearer a portal landing than to the player scores the same from -- every room on the map. That is why these counts do not change when -- you walk somewhere else. local via = "walk" local bp = (type(snd_bfs_path) == "function") and snd_bfs_path(src, dst) or nil if bp and bp[1] and tostring(bp[1].via):find("portal", 1, true) then via = "PORTAL" portalled = portalled + 1 end
local note = via local diff = "" if mh and bh then local delta = bh - mh diff = tostring(delta) if delta == 0 then agree = agree + 1 else differ = differ + 1 if math.abs(delta) > worst then worst, worst_i = math.abs(delta), i end note = via .. ((delta < 0) and " / ours shorter" or " / ours longer") end else unreachable = unreachable + 1 note = (not mh) and "mapper found none" or "ours found none" end
if mnp and mh and mnp ~= mh then np_differs = np_differs + 1 end InfoNote("SnD: ", string.format("%-30s %7s %7s %7s %7s %s", tostring(labels[i]):sub(1, 30), tostring(mh or "-"), tostring(mnp or "-"), tostring(bh or "-"), diff, note)) end
InfoNote("SnD: ", string.rep("-", 60)) InfoNote("SnD: agree ", tostring(agree), ", differ ", tostring(differ), ", no route ", tostring(unreachable)) if portalled > 0 then InfoNote("SnD: ", tostring(portalled), " of ", tostring(#dests), " of our answers start with a portal, which our search allows", " from anywhere -- those counts do not depend on where you are") InfoNote("SnD: standing.") end -- Say plainly whether this run settled anything. Agreement from a room -- that permits portals is the expected result and not evidence either -- way: both sides portal, so both count the same. The comparison only -- has teeth where the mapper is forced to walk out first. if np_differs == 0 then InfoNote("SnD: mapNP matches mapper on every row: forbidding portals", " changed nothing, so no answer here actually depended on one", " and this run cannot separate the two methods.") else InfoNote("SnD: mapNP differs on ", tostring(np_differs), " row(s):", " those routes really do use a portal. In a room that blocks", " portalling, that gap is how much our count understates it.") end if np == 1 then InfoNote("SnD: This room is noportal per the mapper -- if mapper and", " ours still agree, the mapper is not applying the room's own", " flag either, and the shortcut costs nothing in practice.") elseif np ~= nil then InfoNote("SnD: Portals are allowed here, so agreement was guaranteed", " and this run proves nothing about accuracy. Use", " 'xtest noportal' to find a room where it would.") end if multi_leg > 0 then InfoNote("SnD: ", tostring(multi_leg), " of ", tostring(#dests), " mapper routes came back in more than one leg -- it had to", " walk somewhere it could portal from before portalling.", " That walk is the part our count leaves out.") end if slowest > 2.0 then InfoNote("SnD: slowest mapper call was ", string.format("%.1fs", slowest), " (", tostring(labels[slowest_i] or "?"), "). findpath", " searches exhaustively before giving up, and it blocks the", " client while it does -- which is why it is a diagnostic", " here and not something to call while routing.") end InfoNote("SnD: ", string.format("mapper %.3fs total (%.3fs each), " .. "ours %.3fs total (%.3fs each)", t_mapper_total, t_mapper_total / #dests, t_bfs_total, t_bfs_total / #dests))
-- Show the worst disagreement in full: the counts say there is a gap, the -- routes say what caused it. if worst_i then local dst = dests[worst_i] InfoNote("SnD: biggest gap is ", tostring(labels[worst_i]), " (room ", tostring(dst), "):") local mp = routes[worst_i] if mp then local n = 0 while mp[n + 1] ~= nil and n < 15 do n = n + 1 InfoNote(string.format("SnD: mapper %2d. %-20s -> %s", n, tostring(mp[n].dir), tostring(mp[n].uid))) end end local bp = snd_bfs_path(src, dst) if bp then for i, step in ipairs(bp) do if i > 15 then break end InfoNote(string.format("SnD: ours %2d. %-20s -> %s", i, step.via, step.room)) end end end end

-- ─── ASYNC REQUESTS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- One place that loads the async library and issues a request. There were three -- copies of the require before this, each with its own idea of the third -- argument, and download_file guarded on a GLOBAL async_ok that nothing ever -- assigned -- the other two copies declared it `local`. So download_file always -- took its else branch: the changelog, the version check and the plugin -- download all reported "Error on file download" without ever trying. -- -- The third argument has meant different things across package versions. -- Current async.lua treats it as the protocol, asserts it is HTTP or HTTPS, and -- infers it from the URL when omitted. Older copies treat it as the HTTP verb -- and assert on GET/POST/HEAD, so omitting it fails there instead. No single -- value is right for both, so the modern form is tried first and the older one -- used if it raises. Both assert before issuing a request, so a rejected call -- leaves nothing behind. local _snd_async_mod = nil
function snd_async() if _snd_async_mod then return _snd_async_mod end local ok, mod = pcall(require, "async") if not ok then return nil, tostring(mod) end _snd_async_mod = mod async = mod -- legacy global, still read elsewhere return mod end
function snd_http_get(url, callback) local a, err = snd_async() if not a then ErrorNote("SnD: the 'async' library is not available: ", tostring(err)) return false end if type(url) ~= "string" or not url:lower():match("^https?://") then ErrorNote("SnD: refusing to fetch a malformed URL: ", tostring(url)) return false end
local ok = pcall(a.doAsyncRemoteRequest, url, callback) if not ok then ok = pcall(a.doAsyncRemoteRequest, url, callback, "GET") end if not ok then ErrorNote("SnD: could not start a download of ", url) return false end return true end
function download_file(url, callback) DebugNote("Starting download of ", url) snd_http_get(url, callback) end
function check_version_callback(callback, log_no_updates) return function(retval, page, status, headers, full_status, request_url) if status ~= 200 then DebugNote("check_version_callback got ", status) if log_no_updates then ErrorNote("Error while fetching latest version number") end return end local upstream_version = Trim(page) if upstream_version ~= _snd_version_str() then callback(upstream_version) elseif log_no_updates then InfoNote("Search&Destroy: No new updates available") end end end
function do_update(version) DebugNote("Attempting to do_update with version ", version) download_plugin("v" .. version, callback_update_plugin) end
-- Fetch the published VERSION and, if it differs from the running plugin, -- replace the plugin file with that release's copy. -- -- Called at the end of a module update. Version strings are compared as -- strings, never with tonumber(): tonumber("6.0.1") is nil, so anything with -- three parts would compare as "no version at all". -- Replace the plugin file with the copy on `ref`, whatever version it claims. -- -- Releases compare versions first; a dev branch cannot, since its version does -- not change between pushes. Testing plugin-file changes is the main reason -- 'snd dev update' exists, so it always takes the branch's copy. function _snd_update_plugin_file_from(ref) download_file(snd_raw_url("Search_and_Destroy.xml", ref), callback_update_plugin) end
function _snd_update_plugin_file_if_stale() download_file(snd_raw_url("VERSION"), function(retval, page, status) if status ~= 200 or not page then return end local latest = Trim(page) if latest == "" or latest == _snd_version_str() then return end ColourNote("silver", "", "SnD: Plugin file is v" .. _snd_version_str() .. ", latest is v" .. latest .. " -- updating it too.") do_update(latest) end) end
function callback_update_plugin(retval, page, status, headers, full_status, request_url) if status ~= 200 then DebugNote("callback_update_plugin got ", status) -- Almost always a missing release tag: the plugin file is fetched from -- "v<version>", not from the branch, so publishing a VERSION bump -- without tagging leaves every install unable to update itself. ErrorNote("SnD: could not fetch the plugin for ", tostring(_snd_plugin_update_ref), " (HTTP ", tostring(status), ").") ErrorNote("SnD: your modules are current; the plugin file was left alone.") return end -- A string, not tonumber(): tonumber("6.0.1") is nil, which would print -- "updating to nil" and error outright when a beta tag is appended below. -- Read the real version from SND_VERSION, not from the plugin attribute: -- the attribute is numeric and only carries major.minor. local upstream_version = string.match(page, 'SND_VERSION%s*=%s*"([^"]*)"') or string.match(page, '<plugin version="([0-9%.]+)"') or "(unknown)" local pluginVer = _snd_version_str()
-- If the downloaded plugin does not actually carry the version that -- VERSION advertised, every future check will find it stale again and -- update-and-reload on every run. Say so rather than let that loop happen -- quietly. local carried = string.match(page, 'SND_VERSION%s*=%s*"([^"]*)"') if carried and _snd_plugin_update_ref and ("v" .. carried) ~= _snd_plugin_update_ref then ErrorNote("SnD: the plugin at ", tostring(_snd_plugin_update_ref), " reports itself as v", carried, " -- the release is inconsistent and updates may repeat.") end
ImportantNote("Updating from version ", pluginVer, " to ", upstream_version, ". Do not touch anything!") -- Never reload on a write we could not make: that would restart the plugin -- expecting new code and get the old file back, with no explanation. local path = GetPluginInfo(GetPluginID(), 6) local file = io.open(path, "w") if not file then ErrorNote("SnD: could not open the plugin file for writing: ", tostring(path)) ErrorNote("SnD: the update was not applied.") return end file:write(page) file:close() if "" == GetAlphaOption("script_prefix") then SetAlphaOption("script_prefix", "\\\\\\") end Execute( GetAlphaOption("script_prefix") .. 'DoAfterSpecial(1, "ReloadPlugin(\'' .. GetPluginID() .. '\')", sendto.script)' ) ImportantNote("Update complete!") end -- end Update code

-- Reload after a module update, but only when nothing is in mid-flight. -- -- Replacing the plugin file already reloads unasked, so the two update paths -- were inconsistent. The reason to hesitate here is that a reload empties the -- in-memory campaign state -- main_target_list, current_target, the navigation -- queue -- none of which is rebuilt on load. Nothing is destroyed (settings, -- marks, keywords and history are in the database) but mid-campaign it costs -- a 'cp info' to get the list back, and mid-walk it leaves the player standing -- still. -- -- So: reload when there is nothing to interrupt, and otherwise say so and let -- them choose the moment. local function _snd_busy_reason() if type(has_activity_target) == "function" and has_activity_target() then return "you are working a campaign or quest target" end if type(main_target_list) == "table" and #main_target_list > 0 then return "a target list is loaded" end if type(gotoList) == "table" and #gotoList > 0 then return "a route is in progress" end if type(is_character_ready) == "function" and not is_character_ready() then return "you are " .. (type(character_state_string) == "function" and character_state_string() or "busy") end return nil end

local busy = _snd_busy_reason() if busy then ColourNote("silver", "", "SnD: updates are ready, but " .. busy .. " -- type 'snd reload' when you are done.") return end
ColourNote("silver", "", "SnD: reloading to apply the updates...") sndReload() end

function rawCopyPwarDB() local pwar_path = GetInfo(60) .. "WinkleGold_Database.db" local f = io.open(pwar_path, "r") if not f then error( "To start migration process, please locate the file " .. "'WinkleGold_Database.db' and move it to the plugins folder. Then try again." ) end f:close()

local PwarDb = assert(sqlite3.open(pwar_path)) local mapperDb = assert(sqlite3.open(GetInfo(66) .. "Aardwolf.db")) local SnDdb = db_open()
-- ── Step 1: Clear existing mob and global-keyword data ─────────────────── InfoNote("Clearing existing mob data...") execute_in_transaction(SnDdb, function(db) dbcheck(db, db:exec("DELETE FROM mob_sightings"), "pwar: clear mob_sightings") dbcheck(db, db:exec("DELETE FROM mob_kills"), "pwar: clear mob_kills") dbcheck(db, db:exec("DELETE FROM mob_keywords WHERE char_id IS NULL"), "pwar: clear global mob_keywords") end)
-- ── Step 2: Load mob rows from Pwar and collect room IDs ───────────────── InfoNote("Reading Pwar mob data...") local migrateTable = {} local roomsToLookup = {} for row in PwarDb:nrows( "SELECT roomid, mobname, sum(freq) AS count FROM mobs GROUP BY roomid, mobname" ) do migrateTable[#migrateTable + 1] = { roomid = row.roomid, mob = row.mobname, count = row.count, } roomsToLookup[row.roomid] = true end
-- ── Step 3: Resolve room IDs → area key + room name from mapper DB ─────── InfoNote("Resolving room locations from mapper...") local roomsById = {} local id_list = {} for rid in pairs(roomsToLookup) do id_list[#id_list + 1] = rid end
-- Chunk the IN clause to stay within SQLite expression limits. local CHUNK = 500 for i = 1, #id_list, CHUNK do local chunk = {} for j = i, math.min(i + CHUNK - 1, #id_list) do chunk[#chunk + 1] = id_list[j] end for row in mapperDb:nrows( "SELECT uid, area, name FROM rooms WHERE uid IN (" .. table.concat(chunk, ",") .. ")" ) do roomsById[tostring(row.uid)] = { area = row.area, name = row.name } end end mapperDb:close()
-- ── Step 4: Migrate mob sightings → mob_sightings ──────────────────────── InfoNote("Migrating mob sightings...") local batch = {} local BATCH_SIZE = 5000 local function flush_batch() if #batch == 0 then return end execute_in_transaction(SnDdb, function(db) for _, sql in ipairs(batch) do -- Direct exec (no dbcheck): FK violations for unknown zone keys -- are silently skipped so an unrecognized area doesn't abort the -- entire migration. db:exec(sql) end end) batch = {} end
local sightings_count = 0 for _, entry in ipairs(migrateTable) do local room = roomsById[tostring(entry.roomid)] if room then batch[#batch + 1] = string.format( "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO mob_sightings " .. "(mob, room_name, roomid, zone, seen_count) " .. "VALUES (%s, %s, %d, %s, %d)", fixsql(entry.mob), fixsql(room.name), entry.roomid, fixsql(room.area), entry.count ) sightings_count = sightings_count + 1 if #batch >= BATCH_SIZE then flush_batch() end end end flush_batch() InfoNote("Migrated " .. sightings_count .. " mob sightings.")
-- ── Step 5: Migrate keyword exceptions → mob_keywords ──────────────────── InfoNote("Migrating mob keyword exceptions...") local kw_count = 0 for row in PwarDb:nrows("SELECT mobname, areaid, subname FROM mobsubs") do batch[#batch + 1] = string.format( "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO mob_keywords (char_id, zone, mob_name, keyword) " .. "VALUES (NULL, %s, %s, %s)", fixsql(row.areaid), fixsql(row.mobname), fixsql(row.subname) ) kw_count = kw_count + 1 if #batch >= BATCH_SIZE then flush_batch() end end flush_batch() InfoNote("Migrated " .. kw_count .. " keyword exceptions.")
-- ── Step 6: Migrate start rooms → areas table ──────────────────────────── InfoNote("Migrating area start rooms...") local marks_count = 0 execute_in_transaction(SnDdb, function(db) for row in PwarDb:nrows("SELECT areaname, roomid FROM startrooms") do local rid = tonumber(row.roomid) if rid and rid > 0 then -- Ensure the area row exists before updating start_room. db:exec( "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO areas (key, name, source, difficulty) VALUES (" .. fixsql(row.areaname) .. ", " .. fixsql(row.areaname) .. ", 'scrape', 0)" ) db:exec( "UPDATE areas SET start_room=" .. rid .. " WHERE key=" .. fixsql(row.areaname) ) marks_count = marks_count + 1 end end end) InfoNote("Migrated " .. marks_count .. " area start rooms.")

--[[Mob searching]]
-- Parses and dispatches mob search commands. -- Syntax: ms [<here|areakey>] <mob name> [<level>] -- -- First token is treated as a location qualifier only if it is the literal -- word "here" or an exact match for an area key in the database. Everything -- remaining is the mob name pattern. An optional trailing integer is used as -- a level-proximity filter (±LEVEL_WINDOW levels). function onSearch(_name, _line, wildcards) local input = (wildcards[1] or ""):match("^%s*(.-)%s*$") if input == "" then InfoNote(" Mob Search — usage:") InfoNote(" ms <mob> search all areas") InfoNote(" ms here <mob> search current area") InfoNote(" ms <areakey> <mob> search a specific area") InfoNote(" ms <mob> <level> filter by level proximity (\xc2\xb15 levels)") InfoNote(" Examples: ms hawk ms here hawk ms galadon hawk 25") return end
-- Tokenise local tokens = {} for tok in input:gmatch("%S+") do tokens[#tokens+1] = tok end
-- Trailing integer → level filter (only when there are remaining tokens) local level = nil if #tokens > 1 and tokens[#tokens]:match("^%d+$") then level = tonumber(tokens[#tokens]) table.remove(tokens) end
-- First token → optional location qualifier (only when more tokens remain) local location = nil -- nil means "all areas" if #tokens > 1 then local first = tokens[1]:lower() if first == "here" then location = (gmcp("room.info.zone") or ""):lower() if location == "" then InfoNote("*** Cannot determine current zone — no GMCP data.") return end table.remove(tokens, 1) else -- Accept only an exact area key to avoid misidentifying mob words. local db = db_open() local matched = nil for row in db:nrows( "SELECT key FROM areas WHERE key = " .. fixsql(first) .. " LIMIT 1" ) do matched = row.key end db_close(db) if matched then location = matched table.remove(tokens, 1) end end end
local mob_name = table.concat(tokens, " ") if #mob_name < 2 then InfoNote("*** Mob name must be at least 2 characters.") return end
mobSearch(mob_name, location, level) end
-- How many levels above and below the requested level to accept. local MS_LEVEL_WINDOW = 5
-- Query mob_sightings + areas (+ optional mob_kills) and display results. -- mob_name : plain text, matched with LIKE %pattern% -- location : nil (all areas), or an exact area key string -- level : nil, or an integer (area range must overlap level ± MS_LEVEL_WINDOW) function mobSearch(mob_name, location, level) -- Build WHERE clauses local wheres = { "ms.mob LIKE " .. fixsql("%" .. mob_name .. "%") } if location then wheres[#wheres+1] = "ms.zone = " .. fixsql(location) end if level then wheres[#wheres+1] = "a.minlvl <= " .. (level + MS_LEVEL_WINDOW) wheres[#wheres+1] = "a.maxlvl >= " .. (level - MS_LEVEL_WINDOW) end
local sql = "SELECT ms.mob, ms.room_name, ms.roomid, ms.zone, ms.seen_count, " .. "COALESCE(mk.kill_count, 0) AS kills, a.minlvl, a.maxlvl " .. "FROM mob_sightings ms " .. "JOIN areas a ON a.key = ms.zone " .. "LEFT JOIN mob_kills mk ON mk.mob = ms.mob AND mk.roomid = ms.roomid " .. "WHERE " .. table.concat(wheres, " AND ") .. " " .. "ORDER BY " .. -- Tier 0: exact name match (NOCASE collation handles case) "CASE WHEN ms.mob = " .. fixsql(mob_name) .. " THEN 0 " .. -- Tier 1: search term is a whole word at end ("a hawk", "a wounded hawk") "WHEN ms.mob LIKE " .. fixsql("% " .. mob_name) .. " THEN 1 " .. -- Tier 2: whole word in middle or at very start ("hawk master") "WHEN ms.mob LIKE " .. fixsql("% " .. mob_name .. " %") .. " THEN 2 " .. "WHEN ms.mob LIKE " .. fixsql(mob_name .. " %") .. " THEN 2 " .. -- Tier 3: search term is a prefix starting the name ("hawkmaster" with no article) "WHEN ms.mob LIKE " .. fixsql(mob_name .. "%") .. " THEN 3 " .. -- Tier 4: search term is a prefix of a word elsewhere ("a hawker", "a hawkdraugr") "WHEN ms.mob LIKE " .. fixsql("% " .. mob_name .. "%") .. " THEN 4 " .. "ELSE 5 END ASC, " .. -- Within each tier: shorter name first (closer to exact), then most-killed "LENGTH(ms.mob) ASC, kills DESC, ms.seen_count DESC " .. "LIMIT 50"
local db = db_open() mshow = {} local results = {} for row in db:nrows(sql) do results[#results+1] = row mshow[#mshow+1] = { row.mob, row.zone, tostring(row.roomid) } end db_close(db)

" " .. string.rep("\xe2\x94\x80", W_KILL))
-- ── Rows ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── for i, row in ipairs(results) do local bg = (i % 2 == 0) and BG_ALT or "" local lvl_s = tostring(row.minlvl) .. "-" .. tostring(row.maxlvl) local mob_s = ellipsify(row.mob, W_MOB) local room_s = ellipsify(row.room_name, W_ROOM) local zone_s = ellipsify(row.zone, W_ZONE)
local action = "mapper goto " .. tostring(row.roomid) local hint = "Navigate to " .. row.room_name .. " (" .. tostring(row.roomid) .. ")" Hyperlink(action, string.format(" %3d ", i), hint, C_COL, bg, false, true) Hyperlink(action, string.format("%-"..W_MOB.."s ", mob_s), hint, C_MOB, bg, false, true) Hyperlink(action, string.format("%-"..W_ROOM.."s ", room_s), hint, C_ROOM, bg, false, true) Hyperlink(action, string.format("%-"..W_ZONE.."s ", zone_s), hint, C_ZONE, bg, false, true) Hyperlink(action, string.format("%-"..W_LVL.."s ", lvl_s), hint, C_LVL, bg, false, true) Hyperlink(action, string.format("%"..W_KILL.."d", row.kills), hint, C_KILL, bg, false, true) Note("") end

" result" .. (#results == 1 and "" or "s") .. limit_note .. " \xc2\xb7 xmg <#> to navigate \xc2\xb7 click any row to go directly") ColourNote(C_SEP, "", HR) end

-- ─── MOBDEATHS CAPTURE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- xmobdeaths sends 'mobdeaths here' and parses the fixed-width output table. -- Each row is: N - mob_name(39 chars) level(5) area_name(20) killed -- Results are stored in mob_duplicates via mob_duplicates_set().
-- Globals (not locals) so MUSHclient can reliably access them across trigger calls. _mobdeaths_arid = nil -- zone key captured at command time _mobdeaths_rows = {} -- accumulated {mob, level} rows
function xmobdeaths_cmd() _mobdeaths_arid = (current_room and current_room.arid) or gmcp("room.info.zone") or "" if _mobdeaths_arid == "" then InfoNote("SnD: xmobdeaths — not in a known area (no GMCP room data).") return end _mobdeaths_rows = {} -- Enable the capture group before sending so output is captured immediately. EnableTrigger("trg_mobdeaths_line", true) EnableTrigger("trg_mobdeaths_end", true) Send("mobdeaths here") InfoNote("SnD: xmobdeaths — capturing output for " .. _mobdeaths_arid .. "...") end
function mobdeaths_trigger_start() -- Header line matched. Reset rows in case this fires from a manual -- 'mobdeaths here' run while the capture group is already active. _mobdeaths_rows = {} EnableTrigger("trg_mobdeaths_line", true) EnableTrigger("trg_mobdeaths_end", true) end
function mobdeaths_trigger_line(name, line) -- Format: " N - <mob name padded to 39 chars> <level> <area> <killed>" -- Strip rank prefix: optional whitespace + digits + " - " local rest = line:match("^%s*%d+ %- (.*)$") if not rest then return end -- Mob name occupies a fixed 39-char left-justified field. local mob_raw = rest:sub(1, 39) local after = rest:sub(40) -- Level: first integer in the remainder column. local level = tonumber(after:match("^%s*(%d+)")) -- Trim trailing spaces from mob name. local mob = mob_raw:match("^(.-)%s*$") if mob and mob ~= "" and level then _mobdeaths_rows[#_mobdeaths_rows + 1] = { mob = mob, level = level } end end
function mobdeaths_trigger_end() EnableTrigger("trg_mobdeaths_line", false) EnableTrigger("trg_mobdeaths_end", false) if not _mobdeaths_arid or _mobdeaths_arid == "" then InfoNote("SnD: xmobdeaths — no area captured; results discarded.") return end if #_mobdeaths_rows == 0 then InfoNote("SnD: xmobdeaths — no mob rows parsed (trigger may not have matched lines).") return end -- Group rows by mob name. -- count = number of distinct rows sharing this name = number of distinct -- level variants of this mob in the area (used for ambiguity detection). -- levels = sorted list of unique observed levels. local by_mob = {} for _, r in ipairs(_mobdeaths_rows) do local key = r.mob:lower() if not by_mob[key] then by_mob[key] = { mob = r.mob, count = 0, levels = {} } end by_mob[key].count = by_mob[key].count + 1 local lstr = tostring(r.level) local found = false for _, lv in ipairs(by_mob[key].levels) do if lv == lstr then found = true; break end end if not found then by_mob[key].levels[#by_mob[key].levels + 1] = lstr end end -- Write to mob_duplicates. local stored = 0 for _, data in pairs(by_mob) do table.sort(data.levels, function(a, b) return tonumber(a) < tonumber(b) end) mob_duplicates_set(data.mob, _mobdeaths_arid, data.count, data.levels) stored = stored + 1 end InfoNote(string.format("SnD: xmobdeaths — stored %d mob name(s) for %s.", stored, _mobdeaths_arid)) _mobdeaths_rows = {} _mobdeaths_arid = nil end

-- ─── BOOTSTRAP ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Handles module discovery, async download on first install, smart update. -- -- Load priority (dev path takes precedence so source checkout is live): -- 1. {plugin_dir}lua/<file> (dev / source checkout) -- 2. {plugins_folder}snd_modules/<file> (production download) -- -- On first install, any file missing from snd_modules/ is downloaded from -- BASE_URL. seed_data.lua is also downloaded once, run, then deleted. -- -- Smart update (snd update): downloads manifest.json, compares remote hashes -- to stored download-time hashes, and 3-way merges user-modified files so -- local edits survive the update (see the SMART UPDATE section below).
-- ─── PATHS & CONSTANTS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Production module folder (created on first download). -- Modules ship with the release, in snd_modules/ beside the plugin, and that -- is also where updates are written -- so a shipped install updates in place -- rather than being pinned. -- -- The folder is deliberately NOT called lua/. Our module basenames are -- util.lua, constants.lua, settings.lua, db.lua, window.lua and help.lua, -- which is exactly what a personal script folder next to a plugin contains; -- a generic name there means someone else's util.lua can be loaded instead of -- ours. local _snd_prod_base = GetPluginInfo(GetPluginID(), 20) .. "snd_modules/"
-- Where releases before this one put them. Read-only: an existing install -- keeps working and migrates to the new location on its next update. local _snd_legacy_base = GetInfo(60) .. "snd_modules/" -- Dev override: lua/ folder next to the XML file. local _snd_dev_base = GetPluginInfo(GetPluginID(), 20) .. "lua/" -- Remote module source is derived from SND_RAW_URL in the preamble above, so -- there is exactly one place to edit when the repository moves.
-- Full module list in dependency order. local _snd_modules = { "constants.lua", "util.lua", "db.lua", "settings.lua", "characters.lua", "areas.lua", "mobs.lua", "keywords.lua", "targets.lua", "pathing.lua", "express.lua", "navigation.lua", "hunting.lua", "scanning.lua", "history.lua", "window.lua", "settings_popup.lua", "help.lua", "changelog.lua", }
-- ─── HELPERS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
local function _snd_file_exists(path) local f = io.open(path, "r") if f then f:close() return true end return false end
-- Resolve the path to use for a module filename. -- Dev path wins over prod path; returns nil if neither exists. -- The dev path is opt-in, and deliberately so. -- -- _snd_dev_base is <plugin>/lua/, which is only a sensible module source when -- that folder is a checkout of this project. Plenty of people keep their own -- scripts next to their plugins, and our module names -- util.lua, -- constants.lua, settings.lua, db.lua, window.lua, help.lua -- are exactly the -- names a personal script folder uses. Preferring that folder unconditionally -- meant someone else's util.lua could be loaded in place of ours, which fails -- in ways that look nothing like the cause. -- -- Extracting the source zip into a plugins folder had the same shape, with a -- different symptom: the updater never replaces files found on the dev path, -- so every module would be pinned forever while the plugin itself updated. -- -- An empty file named ".dev" in that folder turns it back on. It is gitignored -- rather than committed on purpose -- shipping it would re-enable the dev path -- for everyone who downloads the source. local _snd_dev_enabled = _snd_file_exists(_snd_dev_base .. ".dev")
local function _snd_resolve(filename) if _snd_dev_enabled then local dev = _snd_dev_base .. filename if _snd_file_exists(dev) then return dev end end local prd = _snd_prod_base .. filename if _snd_file_exists(prd) then return prd end local legacy = _snd_legacy_base .. filename if _snd_file_exists(legacy) then return legacy end return nil end
-- FNV-1a 32-bit hash (Lua 5.1 compatible, uses bit library). local function _snd_fnv1a(s) local hash = 2166136261 for i = 1, #s do hash = bit.bxor(hash, string.byte(s, i)) hash = (hash * 16777619) % 4294967296 end return string.format("%08x", hash) end
-- MUSHclient variable name for a module's stored download hash. -- -- Variable names may only contain letters, digits and underscores, and every -- module name ends in ".lua" -- so "_snd_dlhash_" .. fname produced a name with -- a dot in it, which SetVariable rejects. The write failed silently (its return -- value was never checked), GetVariable then returned nil, and the stored hash -- was permanently "". Every module therefore looked changed on every check, so -- 'snd update' re-downloaded all twenty files every single time no matter how -- many times it was run. local function _snd_hash_key(fname) return "_snd_dlhash_" .. tostring(fname):gsub("%W", "_") end
-- Read a file and return its content, or nil on error. local function _snd_read_file(path) local f = io.open(path, "rb") if not f then return nil end local content = f:read("*a") f:close() return content end
-- Write content to path. Returns false if the file cannot be opened. local function _snd_write_file(path, content) local f = io.open(path, "wb") if not f then return false end f:write(content) f:close() return true end
-- Ensure snd_modules/ directory exists. local function _snd_ensure_dir() if lfs and lfs.attributes(_snd_prod_base, "mode") ~= "directory" then lfs.mkdir(_snd_prod_base) end end
-- ─── LOAD ALL MODULES ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- dofile each module in order. Skips modules that cannot be found -- (should only happen during a partial download failure). local function _snd_load_modules() for _, filename in ipairs(_snd_modules) do local path = _snd_resolve(filename) if path then local ok, err = pcall(dofile, path) if not ok then ColourNote("white", "red", "SnD: Error loading " .. filename .. ": " .. tostring(err)) end else ColourNote("white", "darkred", "SnD: Module not found: " .. filename) end end end
-- Point out S&D modules sitting in the plugin's lua/ folder that are being -- ignored, so "I edited the file and nothing changed" has an answer. -- -- Only fires when the dev path is off, since with it on the files are being -- used and there is nothing to report. local function _snd_warn_if_dev_path() if _snd_dev_enabled then return end
local found = false for _, fname in ipairs(_snd_modules) do if _snd_file_exists(_snd_dev_base .. fname) then found = true break end end if not found then return end
ColourNote("silver", "", "SnD: found S&D modules in " .. _snd_dev_base .. " and ignored them.") ColourNote("silver", "", "SnD: the plugin uses its own downloaded copies, which is what keeps " .. "'snd update' working.") ColourNote("silver", "", "SnD: if you meant to develop against those files, create an empty " .. "file named .dev beside them.") end
-- ─── SEED DATA ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Run seed_data.lua once after modules have loaded. -- The file is expected at snd_modules/seed_data.lua (downloaded by bootstrap). -- It self-deletes after successful seeding. local function _snd_run_seed() local seed_path = _snd_prod_base .. "seed_data.lua" if not _snd_file_exists(seed_path) then return end -- Expose path so seed_data.lua can delete itself. _snd_seed_path = seed_path local ok, err = pcall(dofile, seed_path) if not ok then ColourNote("white", "red", "SnD: seed_data.lua error: " .. tostring(err)) end _snd_seed_path = nil end
-- ─── BOOTSTRAP (FIRST INSTALL) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Called by OnPluginInstall. -- If all modules are already present (dev or prod), loads them synchronously -- and calls on_complete immediately. -- If any are missing from prod (and no dev override), downloads them async -- then loads and calls on_complete. function _snd_bootstrap(on_complete) -- Skip dofiles if the script-block eager load already covered everything. if _snd_modules_loaded then _snd_run_seed() on_complete() return end
_snd_ensure_dir()
-- Determine which files need downloading (missing from both dev and prod). local needed = {} for _, filename in ipairs(_snd_modules) do if not _snd_resolve(filename) then needed[#needed + 1] = filename end end
-- Also check seed_data.lua. local need_seed = not _snd_file_exists(_snd_prod_base .. "seed_data.lua") if need_seed then needed[#needed + 1] = "seed_data.lua" end
if #needed == 0 then -- All present — load synchronously. _snd_load_modules() _snd_run_seed() on_complete() return end
-- Need downloads. Require async library. if not snd_async() then ColourNote("white", "red", "SnD: 'async' library not available. Cannot download modules.") ColourNote("white", "red", "SnD: Place module .lua files in: " .. _snd_prod_base) return end

-- ─── FUNCTION EXTRACTOR ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Extracts top-level Lua function definitions by scanning for `function` or -- `local function` at column 0, capturing until a bare `end` at column 0. -- Returns: { [funcname] = full_source_block_string } -- Limitation: the closing `end` must be at column 0 (standard module style). local function _snd_extract_fns(src) local fns = {} local name, body = nil, nil for raw in (src .. "\n"):gmatch("([^\n]*)\n") do if not name then local n = raw:match("^function%s+([%w_.:-]+)%s*%(") or raw:match("^local%s+function%s+([%w_]+)%s*%(") if n then name = n; body = {raw} end else body[#body + 1] = raw -- Column-0 `end` (with optional comment) closes the function. if raw == "end" or raw:match("^end%s*%-%-") then fns[name] = table.concat(body, "\n") name = nil end end end return fns end
-- ─── BLANK-LINE-INSENSITIVE COMPARISON ──────────────────────────────────────── -- Strips fully-blank (empty or whitespace-only) lines. Used only to decide -- whether a user's local copy counts as "modified" -- an added/removed blank -- line shouldn't trigger the merge machinery or a spurious backup. local function _snd_strip_blank_lines(s) local out = {} for line in (s .. "\n"):gmatch("([^\n]*)\n") do if line:match("%S") then out[#out + 1] = line end end return table.concat(out, "\n") end
-- ─── THREE-WAY MERGE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Given original (downloaded baseline), local (user's copy), and new (remote): -- -- For each top-level function in local: -- * Not in original → user ADDED it. -- - Not in new remote → auto-append to new file (safe). -- - Also in new remote → conflict; save to sidecar. -- * In original but body differs → user MODIFIED it. -- - New remote also changed it → conflict; save to sidecar. -- - New remote removed it entirely → can't splice it back into its old -- position; re-append your version instead of dropping it, and note -- it for review (upstream considering it obsolete is worth knowing). -- - New remote left it unchanged → your edit stays LIVE: spliced into -- the merged file in place of upstream's (identical-to-original) -- body, not reverted. Noted for visibility, not as a conflict. -- -- Returns: merged_content (string), sidecar_content (string or nil) local function _snd_merge(orig_src, local_src, new_src) local orig_fns = _snd_extract_fns(orig_src or "") local local_fns = _snd_extract_fns(local_src or "") local new_fns = _snd_extract_fns(new_src or "")
local merged = new_src local appended = {} -- safe-to-append user additions local preserved = {} -- user edits kept live (informational only) local sidecar = {} -- conflicts / notes that need manual review
for fname, local_body in pairs(local_fns) do if not orig_fns[fname] then -- User added a brand-new function. if not new_fns[fname] then -- Upstream doesn't have it: safe to re-append. appended[#appended + 1] = local_body else -- Upstream introduced the same name: conflict. sidecar[#sidecar + 1] = "-- CONFLICT: upstream added '" .. fname .. "' — your version preserved below:\n" .. local_body end elseif local_body ~= orig_fns[fname] then -- User modified an existing function. if new_fns[fname] == nil then -- Upstream removed it entirely; can't splice back into a -- position that no longer exists. Re-append rather than drop. appended[#appended + 1] = local_body sidecar[#sidecar + 1] = "-- NOTE: '" .. fname .. "' was removed upstream, but you had\n" .. "-- modified it locally. Your version was re-appended rather than\n" .. "-- dropped — review whether it's still needed:\n" .. local_body elseif new_fns[fname] ~= orig_fns[fname] then -- Upstream also changed it: genuine conflict. sidecar[#sidecar + 1] = "-- CONFLICT: '" .. fname .. "' changed both locally and upstream — your version preserved below:\n" .. local_body else -- Only you changed it; upstream left it alone. Keep your -- version live by splicing it in place of upstream's -- (identical-to-original) body in the new file. local start_pos, end_pos = merged:find(new_fns[fname], 1, true) if start_pos then merged = merged:sub(1, start_pos - 1) .. local_body .. merged:sub(end_pos + 1) preserved[#preserved + 1] = fname else -- Couldn't locate the exact text to splice (shouldn't -- happen) -- fall back to a conflict rather than silently -- dropping the user's edit. sidecar[#sidecar + 1] = "-- CONFLICT: could not auto-preserve '" .. fname .. "' — your version preserved below:\n" .. local_body end end end -- Functions identical to original: nothing to do. end
if #appended > 0 then merged = merged .. "\n\n-- ─── USER ADDITIONS (preserved by snd update) " .. string.rep("─", 27) .. "\n" .. "-- These functions were added by you and are not part of the standard\n" .. "-- module. They were automatically re-appended during this update.\n\n" .. table.concat(appended, "\n\n") .. "\n" end
-- Build sidecar content (nil if nothing to report). local sidecar_out = nil if #sidecar > 0 or #preserved > 0 then local parts = {} if #preserved > 0 then parts[#parts + 1] = "-- The following function(s) were modified by you and upstream left them\n" .. "-- unchanged, so your version was kept live in the updated file:\n" .. "-- " .. table.concat(preserved, ", ") end if #sidecar > 0 then parts[#parts + 1] = "-- The following need your attention -- review and manually re-apply\n" .. "-- any changes you want to keep:\n\n" .. table.concat(sidecar, "\n\n") end sidecar_out = "-- " .. string.rep("─", 70) .. "\n" .. "-- snd update merge report — Generated: " .. os.date() .. "\n" .. "-- " .. string.rep("─", 70) .. "\n\n" .. table.concat(parts, "\n\n") .. "\n" end
return merged, sidecar_out end

".orig" local backup_path = _snd_prod_base .. fname .. ".backup" local sidecar_path = _snd_prod_base .. fname .. ".user.lua"
local local_content = _snd_read_file(prod_path)

if not local_content then -- File doesn't exist on disk; fresh download. Still validate -- -- a corrupt download must never be written as if it were good. local chunk, err = loadstring(new_content) if not chunk then return "download-invalid", err end if not commit(new_content) then return "write-error" end return "new" end
-- Whether the user edited this file is decided against the .orig baseline -- written when it was last downloaded -- that is exactly what the baseline -- is for. It used to be decided against a hash kept in a plugin variable, -- which meant a variable that failed to persist turned every shipped -- module into an apparent user edit. -- -- No baseline means the file was never downloaded by us: it shipped with -- the release, or was copied in by hand. There is no edit to preserve, so -- it is replaced outright rather than dragged through the merge. local orig_content = _snd_read_file(orig_path) if not orig_content then local chunk, err = loadstring(new_content) if not chunk then return "download-invalid", err end if not commit(new_content) then return "write-error" end return "updated" end

if not user_has_changes or force then -- No real user changes (or force flag): straight overwrite. local chunk, err = loadstring(new_content) if not chunk then return "download-invalid", err end -- Forcing over a file the user actually edited: keep their copy. -- Back up the user's current version before touching anything. _snd_write_file(backup_path, local_content)
-- Validate the merged result BEFORE ever overwriting the user's working -- file. if not commit(merged) then return "write-error" end
if sidecar then _snd_write_file(sidecar_path, sidecar) return "merged+sidecar" end return "merged" end
